A_target.statement:
Let $p_n = 2 n r \map \sin {\pi / n}$ and $P_n = 2 n r \map \tan {\pi / n}$ be the perimeters of the regular $n$-gons inscribed in and circumscribed about a circle of radius $r$.
Then:
:$p_n < 2 \pi r < P_n$
and $p_n \to 2 \pi r$, $P_n \to 2 \pi r$ as $n \to \infty$.

B_source.statement: The [[Definition:Length of Curve|length]] of a curve is the supremum of the lengths of the [[Definition:Polygonal Path|polygonal paths]] inscribed in it.

derived.the polygon perimeters: lower and upper approximations to 2 pi r

object_map.reformulation: Approximate the circumference by inscribed and circumscribed regular polygons, whose perimeters are computed by trigonometry.

validity_conditions: The circumscribed bound uses that a convex curve inside a convex polygon is no longer than the polygon.
Regular polygons suffice because their perimeters already converge to the supremum.
proof_plan:
Each side of the inscribed $n$-gon subtends the central angle $\dfrac {2 \pi} n$, so has length $2 r \map \sin {\pi / n}$, giving $p_n$.
Each side of the circumscribed $n$-gon has length $2 r \map \tan {\pi / n}$, giving $P_n$.

By the source result, $p_n \le 2 \pi r$.
As the circle is convex and lies inside the circumscribed polygon, its length is at most $P_n$; both inequalities are strict for $n \ge 3$.
As $\dfrac {\sin x} x \to 1$ and $\dfrac {\tan x} x \to 1$ as $x \to 0$, both $p_n$ and $P_n$ tend to $2 \pi r$.
